This page presents between-tool comparisons of multi-locus allele frequency estimates. The simulated data are described in [Simulated datasets](../website_docs/data_simulated.qmd). All estimates on this page use the full, 165-target MAD^4^HatTeR panel.

The tools are [naive multi-locus frequency](../tutorials/PGEcore/naive_MLG_AF_AP/background.Rmd), [FreqEstimationModel](../tutorials/FreqEstimationModel/background.Rmd), [MultiLociBiallelicModel](../tutorials/MultiLociBiallelicModel/MultiLociBiallelicModel_background.qmd), and [SNP-slice](../tutorials/SNP-slice/background.Rmd).

For each tool, the parameter set used for comparisons is the one with the highest Lin's concordance. All four tools are compared on the biallelic diversity groups. Naive multi-locus frequency and SNP-slice are also compared on the multi-allelic *PfDHPS/PfDHFR* group.

Lin's concordance, mean absolute error, and the frequency scatter plots use a 1% filter: an allele is included in the calculation only when both the estimate and the simulated frequency are greater than or equal to 1%. An estimate below 1% for an allele simulated above 1% is set to 0. Precision and recall are shown with and without that rule. A call is a haplotype with an estimated frequency above 0.

```{r}
#| include: false
bench_src <- c("benchmark_data.R", file.path("benchmarking", "benchmark_data.R"))
source(bench_src[file.exists(bench_src)][1])
biallelic <- multi_locus_results("biallelic")
drug <- multi_locus_results("drug")
mixed <- multi_locus_results("mixed")
```

## Biallelic groups

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Estimated frequency versus simulated frequency after the 1% filter. The line is equality."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
plot_frequency(biallelic)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Precision and recall without the 1% filter. Precision is the proportion of calls that were correct (i.e., present in the simulated population). Recall is the proportion of simulated haplotypes that were estimated by the tool."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
plot_precision_recall(biallelic$precision_recall)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Precision and recall after the 1% filter. Precision is the proportion of calls that were correct (i.e., present in the simulated population). Recall is the proportion of simulated haplotypes that were estimated by the tool."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
plot_precision_recall(biallelic$precision_recall_filtered)
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  biallelic$metrics,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Lin's concordance, mean absolute error, and detection. Detection is the share of alleles simulated at 1% or above whose estimate is above 0."
)
```
